callReview.totalNote: total of 16,881 calls from Jan 1 to Jan 31

calls.summary: Margaret Ellison called about routine home hospice care for her mother, who has advanced dementia. The agent explained the Medicare Hospice Benefit and confirmed she would owe little to nothing. A new hospice consultation was scheduled for the following morning.

Daniel Foster asked about the palliative care program for his wife, who is still receiving curative treatment for a serious illness. The agent described how the interdisciplinary team coordinates with her existing doctors on symptom relief. Daniel booked a consultation to begin the intake process.

Robert Hayes called about the Veterans hospice program for his father, a Vietnam veteran with end-stage heart failure. The agent walked through VA-coordinated benefits and Medicare coverage. A consultation was scheduled and a veterans recognition packet was noted for the visit.

Patricia Nguyen called to schedule a hospice consultation for her husband, who has severe COPD and frequent respiratory crises. The agent collected his diagnosis, physician contact, home address, and insurance details during intake. A new consultation was confirmed for later that week and Patricia felt reassured.

Susan Carter, an exhausted caregiver, asked about inpatient respite care so she could take a five-day break. The agent explained the respite benefit and availability at a nearby inpatient facility. Susan scheduled a consultation to arrange the stay.

James Whitfield called seeking grief and bereavement support after losing his mother last month. The agent shared upcoming support group times and the 13-month bereavement counseling program. He asked to think it over and did not enroll on the call.

Linda Barrett called with a billing question about the daily hospice per-diem charges appearing on a statement. The agent reviewed the account and explained which services fall under the Medicare benefit. No new consultation was needed and the item was flagged for the billing team.

Gary Simmons, an existing family caregiver, called with a follow-up question about his father's palliative care visit schedule. The agent confirmed the next clinician visit and updated the medication notes. No new services were booked.

Nancy Coleman called about the Veterans hospice program to confirm whether her uncle's service records were on file. The agent could not locate the paperwork and asked her to resend it. Nancy was frustrated by the delay and no visit was scheduled.

Thomas Reed called with a complaint about a missed respite care handoff that left his family without coverage over the weekend. The agent apologized and escalated the scheduling gap to the care team lead. No consultation resulted and Thomas remained upset.

Deborah Klein disputed a Medicare coverage denial for medications tied to her mother's terminal diagnosis. The agent explained the appeal steps but could not resolve it on the call. Deborah asked for a supervisor callback.

Kevin Marsh called to cancel his mother's home hospice services after the family decided to relocate out of state. The agent processed the discharge request and shared transfer options. No new consultation was scheduled.

Angela Ross called upset about a hospice aide who arrived late for two scheduled home visits. The agent documented the complaint and promised a staffing review. Angela demanded a call back from the branch manager.

Harold Pierce called confused about the location and time of a bereavement support group he thought he had joined. The agent found no registration on record and the line quality was poor. Harold hung up frustrated without a confirmed date.

An unidentified caller reached the after-hours line asking about starting hospice care for a spouse and left a brief voicemail. No agent was available and the call rolled to the mailbox. The message was queued for a morning callback.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: The caller's mother is experiencing terminal cancer with increasing pain and decline in mobility, and the daughter is overwhelmed managing care alone at home. She is seeking professional hospice support to improve her mother's comfort and quality of life while receiving trained support for herself as a family caregiver.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects an in-home consultation within the next week to assess her mother's needs, meet the clinical team, understand what daily care will look like, and learn how Three Oaks can provide 24/7 support for pain management and emotional care.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus should have captured the caller's email address before closing to enable automated confirmation and follow-up materials. He could also have briefly mentioned financial assistance pathways and verified insurance coverage type to streamline the intake visit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling Three Oaks Hospice. My name is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, yes, thank you. I'm calling because my mother is at home and her cancer is getting worse. We need help, and I wasn't sure who to call, so I found you online.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so sorry to hear your mother is facing that challenge. We're really glad you reached out. Three Oaks is here to help her stay comfortable at home with our team around the clock. Can I start by getting your name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Of course. I'm Jennifer Hartley, H-A-R-T-L-E-Y.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Jennifer. And what is your mother's name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Her name is Margaret. Margaret Hartley.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Margaret. Thank you. Can you tell me a bit more about what's happening with Margaret's cancer right now and what concerns you most?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Well, the doctors said there's nothing more they can do to treat it. She's having a lot of pain, especially at night, and she can barely get out of bed anymore. I'm with her during the day, but at night I'm so worried something will happen and I won't be able to help.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That sounds really difficult, Jennifer, and I want you to know you're not alone in feeling that way. Our hospice team specializes in exactly this, helping patients like Margaret manage pain and stay comfortable at home, with nurses available any time of day or night. Are you located in an area where we serve?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We're in Dallas, Texas. Is that somewhere you work?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. We serve Dallas and throughout Texas. That's wonderful. So our next step would be to have a nurse visit your home to meet Margaret and you, learn more about her symptoms, and create a care plan. We typically schedule these within the next week. Does that timeline work for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, that would be great. This week would be perfect, actually. Preferably morning or early afternoon.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Let me get some details. What's the best phone number to reach you at?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it, ending in 7493. Jennifer, I'm going to have our admissions team reach out to you by end of business tomorrow to confirm an appointment time. In the meantime, if you need anything at all, our care line is open 24 hours. You can also call me back at the main line and ask for Marcus. We're here for Margaret and for you.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Marcus. I really appreciate this.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Jennifer. Take care of yourself, and we'll talk soon.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Hartley called on behalf of her mother Margaret, who has terminal cancer with increasing pain and immobility at home. Jennifer expressed concerns about managing her mother's nighttime care and was seeking professional hospice support. Marcus confirmed Three Oaks serves the Dallas area, assessed Margaret's needs, and scheduled an in-home consultation within the week. The call was empathetic and action-oriented, though email confirmation and insurance verification were not completed.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, excellent call structure and empathetic tone throughout. You did a great job validating Jennifer's concerns and clearly explaining what our team can do. Two coaching notes: capture the email address before closing so we can send intake forms and prep materials automatically. Also, a quick question about insurance coverage (Medicare, Medicaid, private) helps our clinical team prioritize paperwork before the visit. Strong foundation here.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Three Oaks Hospice, this is Danielle. How can I help you and your family today?
highlights: Thank you for calling Three Oaks Hospice

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Danielle. My name is Robert Hensley. My father is at home and his doctor mentioned it might be time to look into hospice, so I'm trying to understand what that looks like.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so sorry you're facing this, Robert. I'd be glad to walk you through it. Can I ask what your father is dealing with?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: He has advanced COPD. His breathing has gotten a lot worse and he's been in and out of the hospital.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for sharing that. For someone with severe COPD we'd typically start with Routine Home Hospice Care, where a nurse, an aide, and a social worker come right to where he lives to manage his breathing and keep him comfortable.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay. And honestly I have to ask, what does something like that run? I'm on a fixed income and I want to keep it manageable.
highlights: what does something like that run

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a very fair question. Hospice is covered under the Medicare Hospice Benefit, so when your father qualifies, the visits, his medications for the COPD, and the equipment are almost always covered. Most families pay little or nothing.
highlights: covered under the Medicare Hospice Benefit

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's a relief. I'll be honest, I also called Sage down the road and they haven't gotten back to me, so I'm comparing a little here.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Completely understandable, and you should compare. What sets us apart is our team supports your family 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and if his breathing spikes we can move to Continuous Home Care with intensive nursing right there in the home.
highlights: 24 hours a day, seven days a week

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That around-the-clock part matters. One more thing, my sister helps care for him and I'd want her to hear all this too before we decide anything.
highlights: I'd want her to hear all this too

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, we encourage that. There's no obligation and nothing is locked in. We can schedule a consultation where a nurse comes out, evaluates your father, and answers both of your questions together.
highlights: no obligation and nothing is locked in

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, and would that also cover the respite side? I could use a break now and then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, we offer Inpatient Respite Care for up to five days so caregivers like you can rest, and I'll have the nurse cover that at the visit. Could we set the consultation for this Thursday at 10 AM?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works, and my sister can be there then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I have you booked for Thursday at 10 AM. What's the best phone number and the home address for the visit?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's 214-555-0173, and the house is 482 Ridgeway Lane in Dallas.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, you're all set, Robert. Our nurse will call ahead Thursday morning. Thank you for trusting Three Oaks Hospice, and take good care until then.
highlights: Thank you for trusting Three Oaks Hospice

brandConversationRules: Intro + offer: Introduce yourself as Three Oaks Hospice's AI agent here to help arrange a personalized care consultation, mention that our team is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and that most eligible patients pay little or nothing under the Medicare Hospice Benefit, then ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask the key questions one at a time, who the care is for and their relationship to you, the primary diagnosis or condition, the current care setting such as home, facility, or hospital, whether you are seeking hospice, palliative, or primary care, the desired timeline for support, and finally the patient's ZIP code to confirm we serve their area.

Estimate then book: Confirm we service their ZIP code, explain that hospice and palliative care are typically covered by Medicare, Medicaid, or private insurance so out-of-pocket cost is usually minimal, recommend a consultation with a care specialist to review eligibility and needs, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between hospice and palliative care?
qaPairs.answer: Palliative care supports individuals living with a serious illness who are still receiving curative or life-prolonging treatment, while hospice care focuses on comfort when curative treatment is no longer the goal. A specialist can help you decide which fits your situation during a consultation, would you like me to schedule one?

qaPairs.question: Does Medicare cover hospice care?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, hospice is largely covered by the Medicare Hospice Benefit, Medicaid, and most private insurance, so most eligible patients pay little or nothing. I can arrange a consultation to review your specific coverage.

qaPairs.question: How do I know if it is time for hospice?
qaPairs.answer: Common signs include frequent hospital visits, difficulty managing symptoms at home, and a shift toward comfort-focused goals. Our care team can review eligibility with you, may I set up a consultation to talk it through?

qaPairs.question: Where is hospice care provided?
qaPairs.answer: We provide compassionate, personalized care wherever a patient calls home, whether that is a private residence, an assisted living community, or a nursing facility. Let me schedule a consultation so we can plan care around your loved one's setting.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer care for dementia or Parkinson's patients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide neurological end-of-life care for conditions including dementia, Parkinson's, ALS, and MS. A specialist can assess the specific needs during a consultation, would you like to book one?

qaPairs.question: Can you help with cancer patients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our oncology hospice care supports patients when curative treatment for cancer is no longer effective and the focus shifts to comfort. I would be glad to arrange a consultation with our care team.

qaPairs.question: What services are included in home hospice care?
qaPairs.answer: Home hospice includes in-home nursing visits, aide support, medical equipment, and medications related to the terminal diagnosis, along with emotional and spiritual support. Let me set up a consultation to build a plan for your family.

qaPairs.question: Do you provide support for family caregivers?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer inpatient respite care to give caregivers a break and up to 13 months of grief and bereavement support for families. A consultation can walk you through all the caregiver resources available.

qaPairs.question: Is there care available at night or on weekends?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our dedicated team supports patients and families 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I can schedule a consultation to explain how our on-call care works.

qaPairs.question: What areas do you serve?
qaPairs.answer: We provide care across Illinois, Kansas, Missouri, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Arizona, Texas, Colorado, Georgia, and Utah. Share your ZIP code and I will confirm availability and set up a consultation.

qaPairs.question: How much does hospice cost?
qaPairs.answer: Because hospice is largely covered by Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurance, most eligible patients pay little or nothing out of pocket. A specialist can review your exact coverage during a consultation, may I schedule that for you?

qaPairs.question: How quickly can care start?
qaPairs.answer: We work to begin care as soon as possible once eligibility is confirmed, and our team is available around the clock. Let me set up a consultation to start the admissions process.

qaPairs.question: What is continuous home care?
qaPairs.answer: Continuous home care provides intensive nursing during acute symptom crises to keep the patient comfortable at home. A care specialist can explain when this level of care applies during a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer care for veterans?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Veterans Hospice Program provides veteran-tailored end-of-life care and recognition, coordinated with the VA. I would be happy to arrange a consultation to discuss the benefits available.

qaPairs.question: What is general inpatient hospice care?
qaPairs.answer: General inpatient care provides short-term facility-based symptom control when comfort cannot be managed at home. Our team can determine if it is appropriate during a consultation, would you like to schedule one?

qaPairs.question: Can palliative care be given alongside my current treatments?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, palliative care is designed for individuals still receiving curative or life-prolonging treatment, and our interdisciplinary team coordinates closely with your existing providers. Let me book a consultation to review your needs.

qaPairs.question: Do you help with grief after a loss?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer up to 13 months of family bereavement counseling and support groups, typically at no charge. I can connect you with our bereavement team or set up a consultation.

qaPairs.question: What conditions qualify for hospice?
qaPairs.answer: We care for terminal conditions including advanced cancer, heart, lung, kidney, and liver disease, as well as progressive neurological disorders. A specialist can confirm eligibility during a consultation, may I schedule one?

qaPairs.question: Who are Agape, Elevation, and Sage Hospice?
qaPairs.answer: They are sister companies within our group that operate under one mission to deliver best-in-class care across our service states. A consultation can connect you with the right local team, would you like me to arrange that?

qaPairs.question: How do I begin the admissions process?
qaPairs.answer: The process starts with a consultation where our team reviews the patient's condition, goals, and coverage. Share your ZIP code and preferred time and I will get that scheduled for you.

convo.text: Thank you for calling Three Oaks Hospice. My name is Sarah. I see you're interested in care options for a family member. Can I ask who we're helping today and what brings you to us?

Hi Sarah, thank you. My mother has progressive dementia and we're at a point where we need more support at home. Her doctor mentioned hospice might be right for her now, but I'm not really sure what that means or what it would look like.

I'm so sorry to hear what your family is going through. You're asking exactly the right questions. Hospice can be a wonderful option for dementia care. Our team provides comfort-focused care at home with nurses, aides, and emotional support all coordinated together. I want to make sure we connect you with someone who can walk you through everything and answer your specific questions. Can I ask, are you looking at care starting soon, or are you still exploring options?
